implementation: Worker reads current card counts on every dispatch, including recovered turns. Historical published status counts are no longer authoritative for follow-ups.

A private delivery-state revision travels through the worker/computer/tool-host protocol. Old-snapshot text returns an explicit not-delivered receipt with current counts. The runtime applies the new revision only to the next model response, so already-emitted sibling sends cannot bypass refresh.
Warnings and useful questions can be retried through normal SendToUser delivery. No semantic text classifier or automatic replacement of model text is used.

Consecutive treatment batches update the most recent progress row while pending cards remain, until a 10-second idle gap or intervening chat message. Outcome receipts, row edits, queued push body and update events commit together.

Freshness checks apply to both default control and treatment with current worker/computer versions. Progress row updates remain within the opt-in treatment. Approval and signature behavior is unchanged.
